note.title: Networking: DNS, DHCP and NAT
lines: DNS turns names like example.com into IP addresses.
My laptop gets its IP address, gateway and DNS server from DHCP when it joins the network.
DHCP leases are permanent unless you restart the router.
If I can ping 1.1.1.1 but a website fails by name, DNS is the likely problem.
DNS always uses UDP port 53.
Ask Sam how the office router is set up.
The default gateway is where packets go when the destination is outside my subnet.
ARP finds the IP address that belongs to a known MAC address.
NAT lets many devices share one public IP address.
This part took me ages — revisit on Thursday.
NAT is a firewall, so it keeps my home network safe.

cards.prompt: What role does DNS perform in networking?
cards.answer: It converts names such as example.com into IP addresses.
cards.explanation: Line 1 states that DNS turns names like example.com into IP addresses.
cards.label: sound

cards.prompt: What three settings does a laptop obtain from DHCP upon joining the network?

cards.label: sound

cards.prompt: If pinging 1.1.1.1 succeeds but accessing a site by name fails, what is the probable issue?

cards.prompt: Where are packets sent if their destination is outside the local subnet?
cards.explanation: Line 7 states that the default gateway is where packets go when the destination is outside the subnet.
cards.label: sound

cards.prompt: How does NAT allow multiple local devices to access the internet?

note.title: Linux permissions
lines: Every file has an owner, a group, and permissions for the owner, the group and everyone else.
r = 4, w = 2, x = 1, so 7 means rwx.
chmod 644 lets the group write to the file.
On a directory, x means you can enter it.
Root can't read a file whose permissions are 000.
A umask of 022 gives new files 644 and new directories 744.
Practise on the lab VM, not my Mac.
To delete a file you need write permission on the file itself.
sudo runs one command as root, and it is logged.

cards.prompt: According to the notes, what permissions correspond to the number 7?
cards.explanation: The note states that r = 4, w = 2, and x = 1, meaning that 7 equals rwx.
cards.label: sound

cards.prompt: What does the execute permission (x) allow a user to do on a directory?
cards.explanation: The note specifies that on a directory, x means you can enter it.
cards.label: sound

cards.prompt: Under a umask of 022, what permissions are assigned to newly created files and directories?
choices: New files get 644 and new directories get 744
New files get 755 and new directories get 644
New files get 644 and new directories get 755
New files get 744 and new directories get 644
cards.answer: New files get 644 and new directories get 744
cards.explanation: Line 6 states that a umask of 022 gives new files 644 and new directories 744.
cards.label: wrong

cards.prompt: How does sudo run a command, and what happens to the action?

cards.explanation: Line 9 notes that sudo runs one command as root, and the action is logged.
cards.label: sound

cards.prompt: Which three categories of permissions does every file have?
cards.explanation: Line 1 states that every file has permissions for the owner, the group, and everyone else.
cards.label: sound

note.title: Arabic: the definite article
lines: The definite article is ال (al-), joined to the front of the word.
With a sun letter the lām isn't pronounced and the next letter is doubled: الشمس is ash-shams.
ق is a sun letter, so القمر is said aq-qamar.
With a moon letter the lām is pronounced: القمر is al-qamar.
Ustadha said to practise reading aloud.
The sun letters are ت ث د ذ ر ز س ش ص ض ط ظ ل ن.
A noun with ال can also take tanwīn.

cards.prompt: How is the definite article written in Arabic, and where does it attach to a word?
cards.answer: It is ال (al-) and is attached to the front of the word.
cards.explanation: Line 1 states that the Arabic definite article is ال (al-) and is joined to the front of the word.
cards.label: sound

cards.prompt: What happens to the pronunciation of the definite article when followed by a sun letter?
choices: The lām is pronounced and the next letter is shortened

The lām is doubled and the following letter is silent
cards.answer: The lām is silent and the following letter is doubled
cards.explanation: Line 2 notes that with a sun letter, the lām is not pronounced and the following letter is doubled.
cards.label: sound

cards.prompt: According to the note, how is the lām handled when the definite article precedes a moon letter?
cards.answer: The lām is pronounced (for example, القمر is pronounced al-qamar).
cards.explanation: Line 4 explains that with a moon letter the lām is pronounced, as in القمر (al-qamar).
cards.label: sound

cards.label: sound
